photographs.title: Center of the Cosmos
photographs.description: Center of the Cosmos shows New York’s iconic Times Square from above, using a very wide angle to highlight the expanse of the city.

provenance.sourcePageTitle: Open category winners and shortlist: first look

photographs.title: Kem the Unstoppable
photographs.description: Kem the Unstoppable is an elegantly photographed collage portrait, alluding to Renaissance traditions of portraiture.

provenance.sourcePageTitle: Open category winners and shortlist: first look

photographs.description: A mesmerising black-and-white shot of a stream meandering through grasslands into a lake in the distance, taken in Wenhai, Lijiang.

provenance.sourcePageTitle: Open category winners and shortlist: first look

photographs.description: A meticulously composed image of a street vendor selling electronic parts in Akihabara, once Japan's largest electronics town following a period of rapid economic growth in the late 1950s.

provenance.sourcePageTitle: Open category winners and shortlist: first look

photographs.title: Tbourida La Chute
photographs.description: Many of the photographs taken during a traditional Moroccan ‘tbourida’ show the riders firing their rifles. With this image, the photographer wanted to share another side of the event, and show how dangerous it can be when a rider is thrown from their mount.

provenance.sourcePageTitle: Motion | World Photography Organisation

photographs.title: The Whale Raft
photographs.description: The Whale Raft depicts a group of polar bears feasting on the carcass of a whale in east Greenland.

provenance.sourcePageTitle: Open category winners and shortlist: first look

photographs.title: Octopuses in the Sky
photographs.description: Octopuses in the Sky, showcasing elaborate handmade kites at the Fanø International Kite Fliers Meeting, one of the world’s largest kite flying events.

provenance.sourcePageTitle: Open category winners and shortlist: first look

photographs.title: Encounter
photographs.description: Encounter is a tender portrait of two people shot in the intimacy of a bedroom. The photographer wanted to immortalise this moment for the sitters.

provenance.sourcePageTitle: Open category winners and shortlist: first look

photographs.title: Celebrating Football Club Victories
photographs.description: Celebrating Football Club Victories pictures the elation of fans celebrating a win by their local football club by lighting flares in Bandung, West Java.

provenance.sourcePageTitle: Open category winners and shortlist: first look

photographs.title: Ask a Shaman
photographs.description: Ask a Shaman depicts a group of shamans in La Paz, Bolivia, where they play a major role in Native Bolivian traditional culture, shot against the brightly painted local architecture.

provenance.sourcePageTitle: Open category winners and shortlist: first look

photographs.title: Eclipse of Motion
photographs.description: Dian Ji Wu took this photo during summer break in 2024, at Venice Beach Skatepark in LA during golden hour. The photographer captured this image of a skater mid-air, silhouetted against the sunset, expressing the raw energy of that moment.

provenance.sourcePageTitle: Overall Winners 2025 | World Photography Organisation

photographs.title: Yasnaya Elena Aguilar
photographs.description: Yasnaya is an Ayuujk linguist, writer and activist who advocates for language diversity and indigenous rights. Here, Yasnaya is represented with her grandma and great grandma, the pillars of her education and her guides to seeing the world.

provenance.sourcePageTitle: Bilha, Stories of my Sisters by Citlali Fabián

photographs.title: Malena Rios
photographs.description: Malena is a saxophonist, feminist and women's rights defender, originally from Santo Domingo Tonala, Oaxaca. She became the face against women's violence after suffering an acid attack and her campaigns promoted a law to protect women from this type of attack.

series.title: The Anthropocene Illusion
series.description: Over six years, and across four continents, Zed Nelson has explored how we immerse ourselves in increasingly choreographed and simulated environments to mask our destructive impact on the natural world.
series.imageCountNote: 系列张数未从官网逐帧采集，不填估计值。

provenance.sourcePageTitle: Overall Winners 2025 | World Photography Organisation

publicQuotes.speaker: Monica Allende
publicQuotes.text: The jury applauded Nelson’s urgent topic and his ability to translate complex environmental issues into striking visual narratives. The Anthropocene Illusion illustrates a world where the boundaries between the real and the artificial blur, where the wild survives in controlled enclosures, and where human nostalgia for nature is expressed through spectacle rather than action. Nelson’s work compels viewers to question their own role in this paradox and consider the consequences of a society increasingly distanced from the natural world. This timely body of work tells one of the most important stories of our age, and is now more critical than ever.
